clue.text: Christopher gets to talk at length about soldier's item

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for chattering is read backwards

parts.note: to gab is to chatter on and on

explanation.surface: A man called Christopher rambles on about some piece of army kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but asks for the chatter word to be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitbag is the canvas sack a soldier carries personal gear in.

clue.text: In church smeller misses nothing — this included?

definitions.text: In church smeller misses nothing — this included?

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so the zero is dropped from the word for the smeller

parts.note: a nose is what does the smelling
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: In church the nose catches every scent, including this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' drops O from NOSE, leaving NSE. Read as a whole, the clue describes incense, which nobody in church can fail to smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is the fragrant resin burned in church services, which every worshipper's nose detects.

clue.text: Bishop meeting the lady in Paris — lovely female

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
elle is French for she, the lady

explanation.surface: A bishop meets a beautiful Parisian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired one present.

clue.text: Good Scottish girls taking time, most lacking in emotion?

parts.note: lassies is the Scots word for girls

explanation.surface: Fine Scottish girls take their time and seem the coldest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A glassy stare is blank and expressionless, so the superlative means showing least feeling.

clue.text: Talk about King — is male in reform movement?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes round the king's letter

parts.note: chat is informal talk
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for a king

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man discussing the monarch belongs to some reform campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means surrounding here; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was the 1830s-40s British working-class campaign for political reform, named after its People's Charter.

clue.text: Like many a king that's boasted about knight

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for boasted wraps the knight's letter

parts.note: crowed means bragged or boasted
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A king who bragged about one of his knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Most kings have had a crown placed on their head at a coronation.

clue.text: In the manner of fighting force creating fear

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
RM, the Royal Marines, is a fighting force

explanation.surface: Something done the way an army would do it spreads terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety at a threat.

clue.text: Left in hot train, suffering — one needs lots of exercise!

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left sits inside the scrambled letters
suffering means the hot train is in a bad way, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a sweltering train complains about needing a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' scrambles HOTTRAIN and 'in' puts L among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is a race of swimming, cycling and running, demanding a great deal of exertion.

clue.text: Newspaper depressed when shining light leaves

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A journalist gets gloomy as the light fades.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is sunset, the time when the sun's light disappears.

clue.text: Sailor comes to Scottish island with speech — gets folk working together

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives on a Hebridean island, gives a speech and gets the locals cooperating.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in answer order COLL, AB, ORATION, though the sailor is named first; 'comes to' and 'with' just join them.
explanation.definitionFit: Collaboration is joint effort, the state of people working together.

clue.text: Irrationality of internationalists concerning a young man?

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is a body of internationalists
re is a formal word meaning concerning
a son is a young man in relation to his parents

explanation.surface: A question whether globalists are being unreasonable about some youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is a literary word for a lack of rational thought.

clue.text: Something proposed at meeting creating a stir?

definitions.meaning: a formal proposal put to a meeting for debate and a vote
a movement or disturbance, as of something being stirred

explanation.surface: A proposal put to a meeting that causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a proposal tabled for a vote, and physical movement or agitation.

clue.text: A bit of money needed by soldiers in HQ?

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a hundredth of a dollar
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops at headquarters need some small change.
explanation.definitionFit: A headquarters is the hub or centre of an organisation's operations.

clue.text: Skill rising with country losing any number? That's a sort of sign

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for skill reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: losing means the country's name gives up a letter

parts.note: Denmark is a European country
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Talent ascends as a nation shrinks: a portent of some kind?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ART into TRA; 'losing' takes N from DENMARK, leaving DEMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a registered sign or logo identifying a company's goods.

clue.text: Fish, black fish, playing around in the water?

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Fish, including a dark one, splash about in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabbling is dipping and splashing hands or feet in water; the question mark flags the playful sense.

clue.text: Given extra overnight support?

parts.note: a bolster is a long pillow, so in bed at night one gets propped up by one

explanation.definitionFit: To be supported is to be propped up, and the bedtime pillow puns on that sense.

clue.text: Only some in performance left

indicators.note: in tells us the word for a portion sits inside the word for a performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a part is only some of the whole

explanation.surface: Only a fraction of those at a show stayed; the rest went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Only some' must be read as a whole phrase for a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of depart, a synonym of left as in went away.

clue.text: Each artist cum revolutionary can be a pain!

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone who is both a painter and a rebel can be tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like an anagram signal but is CHE; 'cum', Latin for with, just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, and also slang for nagging.

clue.text: Expands various details

indicators.note: various means differing, so the letters of details are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone elaborates on assorted particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilates means widens or enlarges, as a pupil does.

clue.text: See northern fellow in the metropolis

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Spot a man from the north in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Britain is often called simply the metropolis.

clue.text: Be responsible for lines written in Old English

indicators.note: written in means the lines are set inside the abbreviation for the old language

parts.note: verse is poetry, lines of writing

explanation.surface: Taking charge of poetry composed in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' is the container signal: the poetry sits inside the old language's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, having charge of something.

clue.text: Time for the weekend to begin in China

parts.note: Fri, short for Friday, is a day and so a time
the weekend begins at Friday's end

explanation.surface: When does the weekend start in China?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'Fri end': the end of Friday is when the weekend begins. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a pal.

clue.text: Cover doctor placed over animal

indicators.note: in a down clue placed over means the doctor's letters stand above the animal's

parts.note: an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: A medic throws a blanket over a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape is to cover something loosely with cloth.

clue.text: Beaten, showing a white face?

definitions.meaning: covered in white soapy foam, as a face ready for shaving

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed and pale with shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both thrashed and covered in soapsuds, as a face before shaving.

clue.text: Correct person to work on article about soldiers

indicators.note: about means around, so the editor's letters surround the soldiers

parts.note: an ed, editor, works on articles for publication
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: The right person to work on a story about the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'Correct' looks like an adjective but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing errors.

clue.text: Dull, like a blank sheet of paper?

definitions.text: like a blank sheet of paper?
definitions.meaning: bearing no written letters or symbols at all

explanation.surface: Something as boring as an empty page.
explanation.definitionFit: It means lacking personality, and punningly having no printed letters on it.

clue.text: You want the earth? You'd better show this!

definitions.text: You want the earth? You'd better show this!

parts.words: You want the earth? You'd better show this!
parts.note: alludes to the Beatitude 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth'

explanation.surface: A stern warning to someone grasping who wants everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sermon on the Mount promises the earth to the humble, so humility is what earns it.

clue.text: After party daughter is given something valuable — a vehicle

indicators.note: After places the daughter's letter behind the word for a party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a gem is a precious stone, anything prized

explanation.surface: After the party, a daughter receives a precious present: a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a small electric bumper car at a funfair.
